definitions.definition: Avalokiteśvara sees the five aggregates (form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness) as empty (of own-being in the Sanskrit-short text); form is emptiness and emptiness is form, and likewise for the other four; all dharmas have the mark of emptiness, unarisen and unceased, and in emptiness there are no aggregates, sense-bases, realms, links of dependent origination, four truths, knowledge or attainment.

checks.note: Entity read against the teachings it rests on and their segments: faithful; level not raised by J.
